classification.difficultyReason: Plot each supplied line and parabola using graphing software and read their intersection coordinates, recognising the single tangency solution in part (c). Equations and method are supplied, so the task directly applies graphical intersection.

content.prompt: Use graphing software to sketch the following, and hence find the solution graphically.

answer.worked: Plot $y=x^2$ and $y=x$ on the same axes. Read the two intersection points as $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$.

spec.description: Authored software-style sketch with distinct blue quadratic and red line, labelled intersections and a separate equation legend. Unit-spaced ticks and no grid.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2 and y=x intersect at (0,0) and (1,1).

answer.worked: Plot $y=x^2-4$ and $y=x+8$ on the same axes. Read the two intersection points as $(-3,5)$ and $(4,12)$.

spec.description: Authored graphical solution with x ticks every 2 units and y ticks every 4 units, distinct series and labelled intersections. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-4 and y=x+8 intersect at (-3,5) and (4,12).

answer.worked: Plot $y=x^2$ and $y=2x-1$ on the same axes. The line is tangent to the parabola at $(1,1)$, giving one solution.

spec.description: Authored graph showing tangency, unit-spaced x ticks, y ticks every 2 units, no grid and a separate equation legend.
spec.mathematics: The line y=2x-1 touches y=x^2 at (1,1).

answer.worked: Plot $y=x^2+2x+2$ and $y=-3x-2$ on the same axes. Read the two intersection points as $(-1,1)$ and $(-4,10)$.

spec.description: Authored graphical solution with x ticks every 2 units, y ticks every 4 units, no grid, two labelled intersections and a separate equation legend.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2+2x+2 and y=-3x-2 intersect at (-1,1) and (-4,10).
